correctness.rationale: Fourier inversion identifies exact periodic intensities with autocorrelations. Since omega^2+omega+1=0, each autocorrelation has a unique ordered two-integer coefficient key. All 364 global-phase-normalized inputs at lengths 1 through 6 were enumerated with exact integer arithmetic; both independent checks agree on 1,2,4,7,13,30 intensity classes and a sole length-six triple symmetry fiber. The exceptional representative correlations are exactly (6,0,0,3,0,0), and all three canonical orbits have six normalized elements. Finite enumeration is the full stated domain, not a sample. No claims beyond length six are made.

value.rationale: The sharp minimum failing length across all smaller lengths, unique threefold spectral collision, and inability to distinguish a (4,1,1) three-phase composition from a (3,3,0) two-phase composition constitute a motivated and exact boundary in finite-alphabet cyclic Fourier phase retrieval. The result addresses identifiability of phase-alphabet occupancy, a core practical diagnostic, and is not a routine change of alphabet in an existing cyclic classification because the distinct cubic-root cyclotomic relation produces a non-generic cross-composition ambiguity.
